subject: Physics
title: Reflection of Light
summary: The Moon makes no light, yet it shines at night: sunlight bounces off it to our eyes. That bouncing back is reflection.
keyPoints: **Reflection**: light falls on a surface and returns into the **same medium**.
**Luminous** objects make light (Sun, bulb, candle); **non-luminous** ones (Moon, book, wall) are seen by reflected light.
No light, no reflection: in a dark room even a white wall vanishes.

blocks.alt: Sunlight reflected by the Moon towards the Earth
blocks.caption: Sun (luminous) → Moon (non-luminous) → Earth.

options: returns into the same medium from a surface
quiz.explain: That is the definition of reflection.
The Moon makes no light; it reflects sunlight.

quiz.q: In a completely dark room a white wall is invisible because:
options: no light falls on it to be reflected
quiz.explain: No light means nothing to reflect into our eyes.
Smooth, shiny surfaces reflect most of the light falling on them.

simulation.reason: A definition and a classification carried by the Moon example and the dark-room test in the video; nothing to vary.
